what_its_for: Celecoxib is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis (including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis), ankylosing spondylitis (arthritis of the spine), and acute pain such as menstrual cramps. It belongs to a class of medicines called NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) and works by reducing the substances in your body that cause pain and inflammation.
how_to_take: Take celecoxib exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, taking it with food or milk may help. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. If you have trouble swallowing the capsule, you may carefully open it and sprinkle the contents onto a spoonful of cool or room-temperature applesauce, then swallow it right away without chewing. Do not take more than your prescribed dose, and do not take it more often than directed.
dosing: Your dose will depend on your condition and how you respond to the medicine. Common starting doses are 100 mg to 200 mg once or twice daily for arthritis. For acute pain or menstrual cramps, a starting dose of 400 mg may be given, followed by 200 mg if needed on the first day, then 200 mg twice daily as needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary by person and condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store celecoxib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking celecoxib, as it can increase your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) or naproxen (Aleve) at the same time unless your doctor approves, as this raises your risk of side effects. Avoid taking aspirin (unless your doctor prescribed low-dose aspirin for heart protection). Talk to your doctor before using any over-the-counter pain relievers or cold medicines, as many contain NSAIDs. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as some people may become more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of your body, or slurred speech (signs of a heart attack or stroke); black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds (signs of stomach bleeding); severe stomach pain; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; skin rash, blisters, or peeling skin; yellowing of your skin or eyes; sudden weight gain or swelling in your legs or ankles; little or no urination; or severe allergic reaction. Also contact your doctor if you have increased blood pressure, vision changes, or if your pain does not improve.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some pain relief within a few hours of your first dose. However, the full anti-inflammatory effects for conditions like arthritis may take several days to a few weeks of regular use. Let your doctor know if you do not notice any improvement after a few weeks.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use celecoxib during the last 3 months of pregnancy (third trimester) as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Celecoxib may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults are at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart side effects, so doctors usually start with the lowest effective dose and monitor closely. Children: Celecoxib is approved for children 2 years and older with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis; the dose is based on the child's weight. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as special precautions or dose adjustments may be needed. Sulfa allergy: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfonamide medicines (sulfa drugs), as celecoxib may cause a similar reaction.
